NeRF-Neural ODE replaces the discrete quadrature summation of standard NeRF with a continuous Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (Neural ODE) solver to integrate radiance and transmittance along rays [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the notes and code comments that the technique replaces the discrete quadrature summation of NeRF with a continuous Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (Neural ODE) solver to integrate radiance and transmittance along rays. The code implementation confirms this by defining an ODE derivative function that computes the derivatives of accumulated color (radiance) and transmittance, and solving this ODE using the Tsit5 solver.

The outputs are concatenated to 316 dims, passed through `Dense(316, 256, relu)`, three `Dense(256, 256, relu)` layers, and a final `Dense(256, 256)` layer [S1, unofficial].

The claim describes the architecture of the NeRFNet trunk. According to Source [S1], the positional encoding of position (L_o=10) results in 60 dimensions. This is concatenated with the output of a 5-layer MLP (60->256->256->256->256->256). The claim states 'outputs are concatenated to 316 dims', which matches the sum of the positional encoding (60) and the final MLP layer output (256). The subsequent layers are described as 'passed through `Dense(316, 256, relu)`, three `Dense(256, 256, relu)` layers, and a final `Dense(256, 256)` layer'. The source code in `model.jl` confirms this structure: `Dense(316, 256, relu)` followed by three `Dense(256, 256, relu)` layers and a final `Dense(256, 256)` layer. All facts in the claim are present and consistent with the evidence.
